title: Multicast Basics: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: A conference call sends one voice to many people. It doesn't call each person separately. That's multicast.

scenes.heading: The conference call
scenes.narration: Multicast uses a shared group address. Group addresses start from two twenty four, called class D. Hosts tell the router they want to join using I G M P. The M A C address starts with zero one, zero zero, five E. And thirty two group addresses can share one M A C address.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. The source is always a unicast address. I G M P runs between hosts and the router. Several groups can share one M A C address.

items.wrong: The source is the group address
Each group has its own MAC

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Multicast sends once to many. I G M P handles joining. Group addresses are two twenty four and up. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva multicast lab.
